introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Physics, Paper 2 (subject code 0580). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A simple weighing machine was constructed from a uniform metal bar of length $1.5\,\mathrm{m}$ and of mass $7.0\,\mathrm{kg}$. It was pivoted at $0.4\,\mathrm{m}$ from one end, as shown in Figure 1. A bag of cocoa of mass $80\,\mathrm{kg}$ was placed at P.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 1: uniform metal bar PQ pivoted at 0.4 m from P; its weight W acts at the centre of the bar.

incertitudes: Question 2, figure 1 : la figure indique le pivot à 0,4 m de P et le poids W de la barre au milieu ; le sac est en P (texte du sujet). Pour (iv) j'ai supposé que la masse ajoutée en Q équilibre la barre horizontale avec le sac en P, la barre ayant sa propre masse de 7,0 kg (moment de 24,5 N m du côté Q).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate:

(i) The weight of the bag of cocoa. *[2 marks]*

(ii) The moment of the bag of cocoa about the pivot. *[2 marks]*

(iii) The moment of the metal bar about the pivot. *[1 mark]*

(iv) The mass that must be placed at Q in order to balance the metal bar. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Weight $= mg = 80\times 10 = 800\,\mathrm{N}$.

(ii) The bag is at P, $0.4\,\mathrm{m}$ from the pivot. Moment $= F\times d = 800\times 0.4 = 320\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ (anticlockwise).

(iii) The bar is uniform, so its weight acts at its centre, $\dfrac{1.5}{2} = 0.75\,\mathrm{m}$ from P, that is $0.75 - 0.4 = 0.35\,\mathrm{m}$ from the pivot on the Q side. Weight of the bar $= 7.0\times 10 = 70\,\mathrm{N}$. Moment of the bar $= 70\times 0.35 = 24.5\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ (clockwise).

(iv) Q is $1.5 - 0.4 = 1.1\,\mathrm{m}$ from the pivot. For balance, clockwise moments $=$ anticlockwise moments:

$24.5 + (m\times 10)\times 1.1 = 320$

$11\,m = 320 - 24.5 = 295.5$, so $m = \dfrac{295.5}{11} \approx 26.9\,\mathrm{kg}$ (about $27\,\mathrm{kg}$).

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one everyday situation in which a (i) couple is used; (ii) moment is used. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **couple** (two equal, opposite, parallel forces whose lines of action are different) is used when turning a steering wheel, turning a tap or turning a key in a lock.

(ii) A **moment** (turning effect of a single force about a pivot) is used when opening a door, using a spanner to loosen a nut, or using a see-saw.
